肉.meaning: Inside a butcher's <part>frame</part> hang two <part>person</part>-shaped hooks, one above the other, each holding a dripping slab. The butcher waves a cleaver at the window. Nothing in this shop is a vegetable: it's all <kanji>meat</kanji>.
肉.on: The butcher drops a slab on his k<sound>nee</sound>, and a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo bursts out of the clock to laugh.
肉.kun: A <sound>shee</sound>p and then another <sound>shee</sound>p peer through the window and quickly walk away.

半.meaning: A goat's two <part>horns</part> poke up behind a <part>two</part>-plank shelf with a cake on it. A <part>pole</part> drops straight down through the middle of it all, splitting goat, shelf and cake into even sides. Everything is cut exactly in <kanji>half</kanji>.
半.on: The goat licks the <sound>hon</sound>ey off its half of the cake.
半.kun: Halfway through, the goat swaps its half for <sound>na</sound>an, a <sound>ca</sound>rp and a <sound>ba</sound>rbecue rib.

体.meaning: A <part>coat hook</part> stands next to a tall <part>book</part> propped up on its end. Hang a jacket on the hook and trousers over the book, and it looks just like a person standing there. Coat on top, legs below: a whole <kanji>body</kanji>.
体.on: To finish the scarecrow body, you knot a <sound>tie</sound> round the top of the book.
体.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>r drives by, the driver shouts '<sound>Rah</sound>!', and a <sound>du</sound>ck lands on the body's head.

三.meaning: Lay down a <part>one</part> stroke, then another, then a third: a stack of planks like a ladder lying down. A cat naps on each plank. Count the cats from top to bottom: one, two, <kanji>three</kanji>.
三.on: Three cats, but you buy just one ice cream <sound>sun</sound>dae and three spoons.
三.kun: '<sound>Meet</sound> my cats,' says a meerkat, and all three of them sneeze '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'

者.meaning: A <part>stuck javelin</part> stands in the grass above a <part>sun</part>-shaped scoreboard. Who threw it? Nobody saw. There are footprints and a sweaty towel, so it was <kanji>someone</kanji>.
者.on: Someone also left a <sound>shu</sound>ttlecock stuck on the javelin's tip.
者.kun: A <sound>mo</sound>le pops out of the grass and shouts '<sound>No</sound>! Not me!'

旅.meaning: A <part>sail</part> on the left, a <part>diving board</part> on the right, and a <part>slash</part> of rope tying them together. You pack a bag, hoist the sail and dive off the board onto the deck. Wave goodbye: you're off on a <kanji>trip</kanji>.
旅.on: You pack one glass of <sound>Rio</sound>ja for the trip and sip it on deck.
旅.kun: On deck you soak in a <sound>tu</sound>b of seawater, with a <sound>bee</sound>tle as your only crew.

券.meaning: A <part>scarecrow</part> guards the gate of the fair, a little <part>sword</part> tucked under its straw arm. You hand over a coin, and the sword slices a paper strip off the roll for you. No strip, no entry: that's your <kanji>ticket</kanji>.
券.on: Your ticket is for the dog show, so you hand it in at the <sound>ken</sound>nel door.

回.meaning: A small <part>mouth</part> is trapped inside a big <part>cage</part>, and it runs laps along the inside walls like a hamster. Round and round it goes, counting as it runs: one, two, five, twenty <kanji>times</kanji>, until it's dizzy.
回.on: A <sound>ki</sound>te string is tied to the mouth, and the kite circles over the cage with it.
回.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>! <sound>Wah</sound>!' cries the dizzy mouth, as a kanga<sound>roo</sound> spins the cage.

学.meaning: A <part>child</part> sits under a <part>blanket</part> with a torch, long past bedtime. <part>Fireworks</part> of ideas burst over the blanket every time she turns a page. She isn't playing in there: she's trying to <kanji>study</kanji>.
学.on: A <sound>gag</sound>gle of geese honks outside the window, but she keeps on reading.
学.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>! <sound>Na</sound>an, please!' she calls from under the blanket, still reading about <sound>bu</sound>lldozers.
